question: Question linked to image nº10 A 4-year-old and 6-month-old boy with a previous normal psychomotor development, which begins to present multiple episodes of medium disconnection with maintained tone and subtle rapid flashing of seconds throughout the day and learning difficulties in the last months. A waking electroencephalogram is performed. An image of the record is shown during the hyperventilation maneuver. What epileptic syndrome corresponds?

options.opc: Benign partial epilepsy of childhood with centrotemporal tips.

Considering the symptoms and EEG findings, the most likely epileptic syndrome is Childhood Absence Epilepsy (Childhood Absence Epilepsy). analysis: The clinical presentation of a 4-year-old and 6-month-old boy with episodes of disconnection, rapid flashing, and learning difficulties, along with the EEG findings during hyperventilation, align with Childhood Absence Epilepsy (Childhood Absence Epilepsy).
